summary: Prompt human review for a person-centred goals-of-care conversation is supported by a recent emergency attendance for acute kidney injury with potassium 6.2 mmol/L, ECG changes, confusion, vomiting and oliguria, preceded by fatigue affecting daily tasks, reduced intake, nausea and an urgent renal referral. This should not be framed as a prognosis or an assumption that deterioration is irreversible: emergency treatment was given and subsequent blood results show creatinine 64, potassium 5.0 and eGFR 52, while current location, recovery, renal follow-up, function, support and wishes remain unknown.

alternativeExplanations: The severe event may have been substantially driven by dehydration and an acute kidney injury for which emergency hyperkalaemia treatment and intravenous fluid were given.
Blood results four days after the emergency attendance were markedly improved compared with the attendance values, supporting at least partial reversibility.
The record does not establish advanced irreversible renal failure, repeated admissions, terminal disease or sustained functional dependence.
reasonsConversationMayBeInappropriate: An end-of-life or palliative-only framing would overstate the evidence because the acute episode was treated and later renal indices improved.
The patient's current recovery, understanding and readiness are unknown, so timing and wording require clinician judgement.
reasonsNotToOfferFalseReassurance: The emergency event included hyperkalaemia with peaked T waves, confusion and oliguria.
Symptoms and an urgent renal referral predated the emergency event, so the episode should not be dismissed as an isolated benign abnormality.
The latest snapshot does not document discharge status, current symptoms or completion of specialist review.

dataQuality.coverageSummary: The manifest records one successful eligible 15-day snapshot source, zero failed sources and 49 unique resources. This is complete for the supplied snapshot format, but it does not establish that all clinically relevant domains were authored or that the patient's status after the latest entries is known.
contradictions: Demographics report ageAtIndex 82, but birth date 1944-09-23 and cutoff 2026-09-13 imply the 82nd birthday had not yet occurred.
The longitudinal problem list labels CKD as resolved on 2026-02-14, while later encounters and referral describe renal deterioration and progressive CKD.

Renal values fluctuate substantially: eGFR 42 with urea 10.6 and potassium 5.5 on 2026-07-24, eGFR 59 on 2026-08-29, severe acute kidney injury on 2026-09-07, and eGFR 52 on 2026-09-11; context and assay comparability require clinical reconciliation.
